Configure the Netskope Client on iPhone and iPad — which tenant the device enrols against, who the traffic is attributed to, and the Secure Enrolment tokens that authorise it.
The client’s tunnel behaviour is configured elsewhere: SingleSignOn, ForceDisabledSteering, TerminateOnSleepThreshold, the IDPMode / IDPTenant / IDPDomain / IDPScope / IDPpreferEphemeral group, CustomDeviceName, and CustomDeviceSerialNumber go in the custom data of the VPN payload whose VPN identifier is com.netskope.Netskope. Only the keys below are read as app configuration.
The human-readable description of this payload. This description appears on the Detail screen.
The human-readable name for the profile payload. The name appears on the Detail screen and doesn’t need to be unique.

The reverse-DNS-style identifier for the payload. This identifier is usually the same as the TopLevel value, with an additional appended component. This string must be unique within the profile. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The payload type, which each payload domain’s reference page specifies.

The globally unique identifier for the payload. The actual content is unimportant, but must be globally unique. In macOS, use ‘uuidgen’ to generate UUIDs. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same ‘PayloadIdentifier’ and ‘PayloadUUID’ in the old and new profiles.
The version of this specific payload.
The human-readable string containing the name of the organization that provides the profile. This value doesn’t need to match the organization payload value in the enclosing dictionary.

Your organisation’s ID in the Netskope tenant.
Take it from Netskope Deployment Parameters in the admin console rather than typing it by hand.
Hostname of the addon server the client enrols against — addon- followed by your tenant URL.

Email address of the device’s assigned user, which is how Netskope identifies who the traffic belongs to.
Use your MDM’s user variable — $EMAIL in Jamf Pro, {{mail}} in Intune.
The Jamf Pro variable is case-sensitive and must be written in capitals: $EMAIL. A lower-case $email is delivered literally and enrolment fails.

Secure Enrolment authentication token, which proves the enrolment request came from your organisation.
Required when Secure Enrolment is turned on for your tenant; find it under Netskope Deployment Parameters.
This value is a credential. Deliver it in an encrypted profile, never in a plain-text profile committed to source control, and rotate it if it is ever exported in the clear.

Secure Enrolment encryption token, which encrypts the client’s initial configuration.
Optional, and only meaningful when Secure Enrolment is turned on.

How long a per-app VPN connection is held while the tunnel is being established, so a request does not fail in the gap.
Per-app VPN deployments only.
